item.title: From treasure hunting to trust-based trading: this is why flea markets in Denmark are more than just secondhand shopping
item.description: Second-hand shopping, vintage clothing, and browsing through pre-loved treasures are, for many people in Denmark, part of the perfect weekend. Here’s why flea markets are so popular over here and where and when to find them.

item.title: Lars Larsen Group to close ScanCom, 2,300 employees to lose their hobs

item.title: “I want to show that a professional career doesn’t have to look cookie-cutter”: How an international flutist finally makes her debut in Copenhagen 20 years after moving to the city
item.description: After completing her soloist programme, American flutist Christine Clancy did not immediately move on to her planned debut concert. item.title: New sustainable fuel flight route launches Wednesday
item.description: Denmark is the first European country to launch a domestic flight route using 40% sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Operated by Norwegian, the Aalborg-to-Copenhagen route aims to reduce annual CO2 emissions by 3,000 tons. item.title: Messerschmidt drops push for Denmark to leave EU
item.description: The Danish People’s Party (DF) will no longer work toward Denmark leaving the EU, according to chairman Morten Messerschmidt. In his new book and an interview with Berlingske, Messerschmidt stated he does not intend to pursue withdrawal or a referendum.
